title: Grand Rounds Canon — Dual-Pane Case Dissection
description: A journal-faithful grand-rounds layout that splits the slide into a structured patient-history column and a thin-framed imaging panel, anchored by a JAMA-style header carrying case ID, date, and presenting physician. Numbered differentials in body serif beneath the panes keep clinical reasoning legible from the back of any teaching auditorium.
philosophy: This template exists for the clinician who trusts that restraint is its own form of authority. It refuses decorative gradients and icon sets, treating white space as diagnostic silence and serif type as institutional weight. The two-pane structure mirrors how experienced clinicians actually reason — history and imaging held in simultaneous view, not narrated in sequence — demanding that the presenter defend both at once. It is designed for the teaching hospital amphitheatre, not a conference expo hall.
goodFor: Grand rounds and morning report case presentations
Radiology and pathology conferences with a single key CT or X-ray image
Differential diagnosis walkthroughs using numbered clinical reasoning
Journal club slides modeled on JAMA or NEJM case-report formatting
avoidFor: Epidemiological studies requiring multiple simultaneous data charts
Pharma or medical-device pitch decks with mandatory brand color systems
Imaging-heavy sequences needing a grid of four or more scan panels
Lay-audience health talks where clinical layout conventions feel alienating
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the cover leaf of a NEJM case report: austere, unhurried, institutional authority earned through restraint alone. Compositional weight rests entirely in the left text column while the right holds a thin-bordered void — diagnostic silence made visible, foreshadowing what the imaging pane will later contain. Mood is amphitheatre-serious: deliberate, still, and monastic in its refusal of ornament. Avoid any gradient, decorative mark, or visual warmth that would look at home in a commercial pitch deck or conference expo booth.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a 7–8% outer margin on all sides. A full-width hairline rule divides a tight top header band — spanning cols 1–12 and carrying case ID, presentation date, and presenting physician — from the body field below. Title text is anchored in cols 1–7, sitting in the upper two-thirds of the body area; a thin-bordered empty rectangle in cols 8–12 foreshadows the imaging pane, treating absence as compositional intent. Presenter affiliation and department appear in a bottom-left footer, separated from the body by a second rule line.

examples.promptCore: The slide evokes a page lifted from a clinical case journal — cool, measured authority with no ornament. Two panes sit in taut balance: the history side dense with labeled field data, the imaging side sparse and thin-frame-conscious, both demanding simultaneous reading rather than sequential narration. The mood is grand-rounds quiet — institutional gravity conveyed through serifs and white space treated as diagnostic silence. Avoid any gradient, icon, or decorative flourish; restraint is the only permitted visual gesture.

examples.layoutNotes: Twelve-column grid; the patient-history pane spans the left seven columns as stacked labeled field rows (chief complaint, HPI, vitals, labs), while the imaging panel occupies the remaining five columns inside a thin inset rule frame. A full-width JAMA-style header band at top carries case ID left-aligned, date centered, and presenting physician right-aligned, all separated from the body below by a single hairline rule. Numbered differentials run in a single full-width strip beneath both panes, divided from them by a second fine horizontal rule. Outer margins hold at approximately six percent; the inter-pane gutter is deliberately generous, and a page number anchors bottom-right with no footer decoration.
